title: Introduce WASM-based instrumentation shim, upgrade OpenTelemetry, and implement exporter backpressure circuit
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Our runtime observability stack is a source of tail-latency and CPU overhead. The existing native instrumentation paths allocate spans per-request, use a sync JSON logger in hot code paths, and rely on an OpenTelemetry exporter implementation with no adaptive backpressure. This causes CPU spikes during traffic bursts and observed retries against the exporter sink which amplify load. Goal: Reduce per-request allocation and CPU cost, upgrade OpenTelemetry to a supported version, and introduce an adaptive exporter backpressure circuit to prevent exporter overload. We will also prototype a small WASM-based instrumentation shim to decouple language-specific hooks from the core runtime and reduce library dependency footprints.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK/deps to >=1.12 across runtime and agent without breaking trace context propagation
Reduce average span allocation per request by >=40% on our standard LLM inference benchmark
Introduce exporter backpressure circuit: exporter should shed or queue with bounded memory and prevent more than 5% increase in p95 token latency under 3x traffic spike
Provide a WASM shim prototype that can be loaded into the runtime and emit spans/metrics with <5% overhead compared to native fastpath for an empty-span case
CI e2e regression tests and a benchmark report are added and green before merge
tasks: Create rollout plan and compatibility matrix for OTEL upgrade
Add per-worker span object pool and zero-copy attribute builder
Replace sync JSON logger calls in hot paths with buffered binary encoder (backed by ring buffer)
Implement exporter backpressure circuit + metrics (queue_depth, shed_count, timeouts)
Prototype WASM instrumentation shim and example loader API
Add benchmark harness to reproduce baseline and post-change numbers
Instrument rollout with feature flag + canary and runtime telemetry dashboard
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Patel: Created ticket after spike during weekend incident. Initial perf numbers attached to design doc. Decided scope: OTEL upgrade + exporter circuit + WASM shim prototype.
2026-03-03 Liam Chen: Spike reprobed locally. Baseline: 18% CPU spend attributed to tracing hotpath and 24 allocations/request. p95 token latency rises by ~12% under synthetic 2x load.

2026-03-05 Design review - Sofia Ramos: Approved WASM shim direction but requested a security review for module loading and sandboxing boundaries. Marking security_review_required=true if shim expands.

2026-03-06 Engineering note - Liam Chen: Implemented per-worker span pool and zero-copy attribute builder in branch otel-pool. Local microbenchmark shows allocations down to 10/request (~58% improvement). Added unit tests for pool lifecycle.
2026-03-08 PR opened: runtime#1428. Replaced sync logger calls in tokenizer hot path with ring buffer + binary encoder. Observed reduced syscall rate and lower GC pressure in dev cluster.

2026-03-09 Performance tests: bench harness run against canary. Results: avg CPU per inference reduced from 1.92 vCPU to 1.34 vCPU (-30%). p95 token latency under 3x traffic increased only 3% with exporter circuit enabled vs 15% previously.

2026-03-10 Ops: Deployed canary to 5% traffic with feature flag. No customer-facing errors; shed_count metric spikes briefly during synthetic traffic as expected. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted.
2026-03-11 Security review request filed: https://tickets.redwood.ai/SEC-9975. Security team asks for WASM runtime restriction docs and KMS usage for exporter credentials; small follow-ups added.

2026-03-12 Liam Chen: Merging per-worker pool and exporter circuit after addressing review comments. WASM shim remains a prototype behind a feature flag; plan follow-up ENG for hardened loadable module path. Added follow-up subtasks in dependencies.
followups: Create ENG to harden WASM loader and run security gating
Add long-term telemetry retention for exporter shed metrics
notes: Trade-offs: choosing a WASM shim reduces language SDK churn but adds complexity for sandboxing and binary size. We prioritized fast perf wins (pooling + ring-buffer logger + exporter circuit) and kept the shim behind a feature flag. Will revisit full rollout after security sign-off and runtime fuzzing.
estimated_impact: Expect 20-35% reduction in tracing-related CPU costs and improved stability during traffic spikes.
